messages.subject: grid.clip and ggplot2
parts:
Although is a subject from a year ago, I am facing may be a similar

one but I am unable to solve it.

Basically I am unable to clip subplots to their specific viewports

within a grid.layout. Specifically if I use highly negative values in

plot.margin (I do it to join successive plots) for a particular side

of a subplot it invades the nearby viewport and hide it if it is in

it's left side.

Does some know if this is a misunderstanding from my side of using

plot.margin with viewports or is it due to the clip option which is by

default "inherit"

I tried to change the default clip argument to "on" but without

success. Is there anyway to fix it?

 

For grid.layout I used a code from Learning R web page, something like

the following (where I tried clip="on" on both viewport functions)

 

Layout <- grid.layout(nrow = 3, ncol = 2, widths = unit(c(1, 1),

c("null", "null")), heights = unit(c(1, 1, 1), c("null", "null",

"lines")))

grid.show.layout(Layout)

vplayout <- function(...) { grid.newpage()

pushViewport(viewport(layout = Layout, clip="on"))

}

subplot <- function(x, y) viewport(layout.pos.row = x, layout.pos.col

= y, clip="on")

Fig <- function(a, b, c, d) { vplayout()

print(a, vp=subplot(1,1))

print(b, vp=subplot(1,2))

print(c, vp=subplot(2,1))

print(d, vp=subplot(2,2))

grid.text("Days after anthesis", gp=gpar(fontsize=10), vp=subplot(3,

1:2))

}

Fig(t06, t07, rh06, rh07)

 

Thanks for your help

Afif

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: grid.clip and ggplot2
parts:
Hi,

I think it's a limitation of Grid's clipping mechanism; AFAIK you
cannot clip a grob that contains new viewports.
That being said, I'm not sure why you should need negative margins?

library(gridExtra)
my.opts = opts(plot.margin=unit(c(0,-0.5,0,-0.5),"lines"),
axis.title.y=theme_blank(), axis.text.y=theme_blank() )
lp = replicate(4,qplot(1,1) + my.opts,simplify=F)
do.call(grid.arrange, c(lp, sub="Days after anthesis"))


HTH,

baptiste
